findings: The all-six direct Together perturbation rejects the core claim that SymbolLeaf and EmptyLeaf share Java's direct-node ordering. Java preserves the declaration order through Cluster#printTogether; Rust moves the ordinary empty package ahead of the six explicit symbol leaves, changing the canvas and all downstream positions.

The valid non-symbol-stereotype control rejects the claimed ordinary branch fidelity: symbol-free empty package emission does not preserve the Java placement of an ordinary package's visible stereotype.

The five passing valid held-outs show that symbol geometry itself generalizes across root/nested ownership, TB/LR, renamed labels, a filled neighbor, all six symbols, and a simple folder-plus-ordinary Together case. They do not outweigh the two fresh counterexamples.

Static inspection found no fixture-shaped code, golden-data reads, coordinate-keyed SVG surgery, unexplained high-precision parity constant, baseline edit, or guard/comparator modification in the audited mechanism. The rejection is a model-completeness failure, not an overfit finding.
All generated SVGs are well-formed XML. Two exploratory inputs have Java syntax-error SVGs and are explicitly excluded; every valid Java pair is retained, including both failing counterexamples.
